passages.t: A fountain opened, and false prophecy removed
passages.happening:
‘On that day a fountain will be opened to the house of David and the people of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and impurity’ (verse 1). God will erase the names of the idols from the land and remove the false prophets and the spirit of impurity (verse 2).

If anyone still prophesies falsely, the text says his own parents will turn on him for lying in the LORD's name (verse 3). These notes name the verse and do not repeat its words. Every prophet will be ashamed of his vision and will not put on a hairy cloak to deceive (verse 4). He will say he is not a prophet but a farmer (verse 5). If asked about the wounds on his body, he will say he got them in the house of his friends (verse 6).
passages.hearers:
The fountain follows the mourning of chapter 12. Those who grieved over the one they pierced are washed clean. Water for cleansing from impurity was part of the law's rites, and the fountain makes cleansing permanent and open.

The verses on false prophecy picture a future in which lying in God's name has ended so completely that would-be prophets deny they ever were one. A hairy cloak was the mark of a prophet, as Elijah wore one. The wounds on the chest may be marks of self-wounding in pagan prophetic rites, like those of the prophets of Baal on Carmel, which the man tries to explain away.
passages.later: Ezekiel promised, ‘I will also sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean’ (Ezekiel 36:25). The law dealt with a false prophet in Deuteronomy 13:1-5 and 18:20, and Elijah wore a garment of hair (2 Kings 1:8).
passages.hard:
Does verse 3 really command parents to kill their own child for false prophecy?

The verse applies the law of Deuteronomy 13 and 18, and on its surface it pictures exactly that. Readers respond in a few ways. Many interpreters take it as prophetic exaggeration: in God's future, loyalty to the truth will run so deep that even the closest bond will not shelter a lie spoken in God's name, and the next verses show the result, prophets so ashamed they deny ever having been one. Others read it as the covenant law taken seriously at last, within Israel's setting as a nation under God's direct rule, not a rule for families in any other time. Christians also note that the New Testament handles false teaching by exposure, discipline and exclusion from the church, never by violence. Across these readings, the chapter treats lying in God's name as among the gravest of sins.

No one is given a warrant here to harm a child or anyone else over religion.

A word for anyone who was not protected by a parent, or was handed over to harm by someone who should have kept them safe. This story does not call that right. What was done to you was wrong, and it was not your fault. If you are still in danger, please tell someone you trust and get help. The Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.
passages.asks: God promises a fountain to wash away sin and impurity. Ask what you need God to wash clean. And ask how seriously you take speaking for God, in what you say about him to others.

passages.t: Strike the shepherd, and a refined remnant
passages.happening:
‘Awake, O sword, against My Shepherd, against the man who is My Companion, declares the LORD of Hosts. Strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered, and I will turn My hand against the little ones’ (verse 7).

In all the land two-thirds will be cut off and perish, but a third will be left (verse 8). ‘This third I will bring through the fire; I will refine them like silver and test them like gold’ (verse 9). They will call on God's name and he will answer them; he will say they are his people, and they will say that the LORD is their God.
passages.hearers:
The shepherd struck here is God's own, the man who is his companion, close to him. The sword is summoned by God himself. When the shepherd falls, the sheep scatter.

The refining picture comes from metalwork. Silver and gold were heated in a furnace so that the waste could be skimmed off, leaving the pure metal. The remnant that comes through the fire is purified, not destroyed.

The chapter ends with the covenant renewed in both directions: God says they are his people, and they say the LORD is their God.
passages.later: On the night of his arrest Jesus quoted this verse: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered’ (Matthew 26:31; compare Mark 14:27). Malachi pictures God as a refiner of silver (Malachi 3:3).
passages.asks: The remnant is refined in fire like silver. Ask what hard season in your life may have been refining you. And ask what it would mean to call on God's name and trust that he will answer.
